summary.text: Ben Ambrose is a 20-year U.S. Marine Corps infantry veteran from Hesperia, Michigan, and the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 2nd District. After his military service he worked as a federal employee for Oregon Sen. Ron Wyden, and he describes his campaign as a return to public service.

paragraphs.text: Ambrose was born in Muskegon and grew up on a farm in Hesperia, Michigan, according to his campaign website; WCMU also describes him as a Hesperia native.
His campaign website says he holds a B.A. in international affairs from Georgetown University and an MBA from Johns Hopkins University.
Ambrose served in the U.S. Marine Corps for 20 years as an infantryman.

In a 9&10 News candidate questionnaire he said he enlisted six days after high school graduation and deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan, with humanitarian missions to Haiti and Marine Expeditionary Unit deployments.
After his military career he worked as a federal employee for Oregon Democratic Sen. Ron Wyden, according to WCMU.
In the same questionnaire he said he testified before the Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee about cuts by the Department of Government Efficiency, which he said led him to run.
Ambrose won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 44.3% of the vote, ahead of Jamie Hill (42.3%) and Clyde Welford (13.4%).
